written.myAnswer: Stability is improved by lowering the centre of gravity and widening the base of support.

An object is more stable when its centre of gravity is low and the vertical line through it remains within its base of support. For example, a racing car has a low centre of gravity, making it less likely to topple. Widening the base enlarges the area within which the centre of gravity’s vertical line can fall, so the object can tilt further before toppling.
The taller box is more likely to tumble because its centre of gravity is higher, so a smaller tilt can bring the vertical line through it outside its base of support.

Stability can be improved by lowering an object’s centre of gravity or widening its base. For example, a racing car is built low to the ground, and a wide-based object is harder to topple than a narrow-based one.
